scope: Qualitative visual inspection, not an annotated accuracy test
selection: Longest example of each of four emitted event types in the 94-recording intermediate snapshot, plus the longest head-change and no-face events after all 138 recordings completed
review_material: Six still frames per example, including a baseline frame and event boundary/interior frames; raw videos and contact sheets stay local

findings.relative_head_change: Visible head/posture reorientation is plausible, but neither its physical angle nor its cause is independently labeled.
findings.relative_gaze_change: Eye/head direction visibly varies; the footage does not establish what screen region or resource was being viewed.
findings.no_face_detected: The candidate remains in view in inspected event frames, including partial occlusion/shadow. Missing detection cannot be interpreted as the candidate leaving.
findings.multiple_faces: Only one face is visibly apparent in the inspected event stills. This is a possible detector false alarm, not verified additional-person presence.
findings.opening_baseline_contamination: In the full-cohort long head-change example, the opening baseline shows the candidate looking down and writing; later upright answering is marked as a long change. An unlabeled opening window cannot be assumed to be a valid normal-answering reference.
findings.non_answer_segments: The full-cohort longest no-face event includes standing up and an empty chair, followed by a return to the seat. Files include non-answer periods; those periods should not enter interview-answer event-rate or AI-use evaluation.

next_validation: Independent timestamp annotations and full clips, including randomly sampled unflagged periods, are needed for event error rates.
